proceedings bearing case no. 2650/2013 pending against the petitioner in the court of Metropolitan
Magistrate No.12, Jaipur city, Jaipur (re-registered as cr.case no. 318/2017) under the Penal

sentences.text: Brief facts giving rise to the filing of instant criminal misc. petition are that on 10.3.2010, the then Food Inspector did an inspection of the shop styled as "M/s. Basant Kirana & General Store" whose proprietor happens to be the petitioner Shankar lal.

During the course of inspection, samples of Jayanti Brand Gutkha were taken by the Inspector and thereafter the same were sent (2 of 4)
[CRLMP-2258/2020] for testing to Health laboratory, Jaipur.

In the report dated 18.4.2010 prepared by the Health Laboratory, Jaipur, the seized material was found to be adulterated and mis-branded, therefore, after getting prosecution sanction on 25.8.2010, criminal complaint came to be submitted before the Judicial Magistrate for initiating proceedings and to conduct trial of the Shankar Lal Agarwal S/O Sita Ram Agarwal vs State Of Rajasthan on 4 January, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64500421/
1 petitioner under the provisions of Section 7 read with Section 16 of the Act of 1954.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The cognizance of the offence was taken by the Judicial Magistrate.

On 21.10.2010 on an application preferred on behalf of the petitioner under Sub-Section (2) of Sec. 13 of the Act of 1954, the learned Magistrate directed to send the sample for the purpose of testing by Central Laboratory vide order dated 10.3.2011.

It is revealing from the perusal of order-sheet submitted along with the petition that since 10.3.2011 to till date, on several occasions, directions were given to the prosecution to produce the sample in the court so that same can be sent for re- analyzing by the Central Laboratory as per mandate of sub-section (2) of Sec. 13 of the Act of 1954, but to the utter dismay, the sample has never been produced before the court by the prosecution.
As a matter of fact, the shelf-life of the seized material i.e. "Jayanti Gutkha" is not more than two months.

Now more than ten years have elapsed; the seized material has surely been deteriorated and now further examination of such sample would become meaningless and thereby the accused has been deprived of valuable right conferred upon him by way of Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954.

[CRLMP-2258/2020] It is apparent that the accused at the earliest possible opportunity had exercised his option for challenging the report of Public Analyst and had prayed to the trial court for sending the second sample of the seized article for analysis by the Central Food Laboratory.

Now nearly 11 years have passed since the sample was taken from the petitioner's Business premises,
hence prayer for re-analyzing the sample has become fruitless in view of presumed fact that the sample must have been deteriorated and won't be in good condition to be tested again by the Central Food laboratory.

The endeavour for sending the sample for further analysis by the Central Food Laboratory would be redundant in view of interval of long 11 years, therefore, this court is of the opinion that for such lapse of more than 11 years, there would be no justification for the trial court to wait for re-sending the sample of the seized Gutkha article for further analysis to be done under sub-section (2) of Section 13 of the Act of 1954 as the same would be a futile exercise.

No useful purpose would be served by permitting the second sample of the article to be sent to Central Food Laboratory, therefore, there appears no option left now with this court but to quash the proceedings against the petitioner as being violative of his valuable fundamental & statutory right to have second sample analyzed from Central Food Laboratory and so also on the ground that the trial of this case has already gone on for a period of more than 11 years since the sample was taken as the same certainly infringes the fundamental right of the accused to have right of expeditious trial guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

(2009(15) SCC,
64)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the fact that shelf-life of the product was not beyond 02 months as the samples were drawn on 10.3.2010 by the Food Inspector, the period of 11 years have elapsed and the sample must have been deteriorated, the continuation of the proceedings against the petitioner would surely be an abuse of process of court and, therefore, the instant petition deserves to be allowed.
